questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wished for the cheapest option and I got it. A lot was broken (bed, window, fridge, washing maschine). the kitchen was filled with flies, dirt and cockroaches, and the baths and bathrooms didn't get cleaned properly. I tried complaining to the person in charge of my dorm, and I got the answer that the baths did get cleaned everyday, but the problem was that the people living in my dorm were "disgusting". At some point I learnt to deal with it, and it's been okay living here because I knew it was temporary. The rent was only 220 euros, which is why I don't rate it worse.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You get absolutely no guide how to navigate the German university system, which is the biggest bureaucratic nightmare I have ever experienced!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to look through HeiCo for courses, then you either have to sign up on HeiCo, and mostly it's not possible, so you have to write the professor in charge of the course, and maybe the professor replies you have to sign up for the course in HeiCo, even though you can't, and then you just have to show up to the class, write your name on a piece of paper and hope for the best. That's just the beginning, because afterwards you have to ask your professor how many ECTS the course is, and they don't know most of the time, and then you have to figure it out yourself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just show up to the classes you want and talk to the professor in person. Don't stress too much in the beginning of the semester about courses, the important thing is having an agreement with your professor and signing up for the exam at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took almost all of my courses in German, which is my third language, which of course made the level harder, and I also took courses outside my own subject, so it's difficult to say something about the generel level. 
But if I have to say something, I did find it similar to the level at UCPH, maybe a bit easier. The workload was way overboard though, I had to do way more work for less ECTS than I'm used to, and not always in a way I felt taught me more.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar with seminar, presentations, lectures etc. The teaching at UCPH is more interactive and less infantilizing. In a lot of my courses they took attendance and you had to "prove", you had done your homework like in high school.
